title: Recovery: pre-approved, and a plan that survives a pulled plug
summary: Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25: the lab manager would pull the circuit breaker about 45 minutes before an exam or essay was due; if you had not saved your work and planned your recovery, it was on you. And: the disappearance of a node is just that, something the cluster grid deals with. Rule (approved by Tom Dyer with "continue", 2026-11-25): recovery steps - FENCE_ROLE, ROUTE_SERVICE of a role or a dead MU's service, ACTIVATE_TASK or START_TASK of what existed - are pre-approved: they run without waiting, are logged with their cause and reported. A recovery step may only restore what existed; a plan that would add capacity or change exposure (swap, a new cache, swapping out other work, a DNS repoint) drops back to NEEDS TOM'S DIRECT APPROVAL and says why. The rule covers the arbitrator's own plans; it changes nothing about orders sent to Codex or anyone else. muDown is a RECOVERY plan and restores a dead MU's services restore only (same site, then home zone, then anywhere). PlanRunner journals a machine plan (PLAN, BEGIN, numbered ledger snapshot with the step it is through, DONE, END) through an effector; resume after a pulled plug performs an in-doubt step again only if its effect is absent and applies it to the ledger only if the ledger lacks it; torn journal lines and torn snapshots are ignored and the next record starts on its own line. Progress goes through oorexx_logging v0.7. dev4: the same runner carries cluster and recovery plans: the ClusterArbitrator answers completed, snapshotLines (every MU with its ledger and holdings, services with rules, role pairs with epochs) and restoreFromLines; a snapshot is written before step 1; the LDAP failover plus site restore survives the plug pulled before, during and after steps, resumed by a cluster arbitrator that remembers nothing (SimulatedCluster stands in for the machines, routes and epochs).
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
